record.text: A project reconstructed how often severe river floods struck the western Mediterranean over the past hundreds to thousands of years by reading layers of mud that had built up on lake bottoms, instead of relying on gauge measurements. How did its researchers work out which of those buried layers a flood had left behind?
record.reference_answer: The project (FLOODARC) picked out past flood deposits in cores drilled from Iberian lakes: after describing the cores, the team cut thin sections and used a state-of-the-art protocol that combined detailed microfacies analyses with geochemical analyses to identify the flood layers. The records built this way ran from the last centuries in the Western Ebro Basin (NE Spain) to the last 26000 years in NW Spain.

record.text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
record.reference_answer: Both projects treat the protective power as something written into the sequence itself and go after it with very large libraries plus machine learning. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which turn into vitrified solids by glass-transition and gelation and so stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and clumping; it computes the sequence features of known CAHS proteins, designs a library that samples that sequence space, screens it with a high-throughput survival assay, checks hits in vitro and in vivo, and feeds the results to machine-learning algorithms to extract the features behind protective glass-transition and then design a fresh library. FLINDIP attacks the same sequence-to-function link from the mutation side, building cell libraries that express hundreds of thousands of variants of tardigrade proteins needed to survive complete drying and scoring every variant by competition assay, again with machine learning used to model variant fitness and design new functional disordered proteins. FLINDIP reported that the phenotype of its original target genes, published by another lab, could never be reproduced, so it moved to different genes, and its delivered result so far is a reusable machine-learning analysis pipeline built on a similar mutation-versus-phenotype dataset from the Kondrashov lab.

evidence:
Gold 838945 - acronym "Desiccation Survival", title "Discovery of intrinsically disordered sequences conferring desiccation survival". Objective, verbatim: "Desiccation is a form of stress wherein extremely dry conditions cause intracellular proteins to unfold and aggregate irreversibly, resulting in cell-death. ... Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins, a family of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in tardigrades (a phylum of micro-animals), have been shown to be important for their survival during long periods of dryness. Under desiccation condition, CAHS proteins undergo glass-transition and gelation to form vitrified solids that protect intracellular proteins from unfolding and aggregation. However, the features of CAHS proteins that confer protection are unknown. Here, I aim to unravel the sequence determinants of CAHS protein functions ... I will (i) perform computational analysis of existing CAHS proteins to extract their sequence features to design a library for adequate sampling of the sequence space; (ii) screen the library with a high-throughput survival-based assay and validate the hits both in vitro and in vivo; (iii) analyse the results with machine learning algorithms to generate characteristic sequence features underlying protective glass-transition. The learned features will be tested by rationally designing and screening a new sequence library for desiccation survival."

Gold 898203 - acronym "FLINDIP", title "Fitness landscape of intrinsically disordered proteins". Objective, verbatim: "The aim of this project is to experimentally measure and analyse, for the first time, the genotype-to-phenotype connection for several intrinsically disordered proteins by deep mutational scanning. We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation. We plan to generate libraries of cells expressing hundreds of thousands of variants of these proteins and to perform competition assays to measure functionality of every variant in the library. We will then use a variety of approaches to analyse the dataset, including machine-learning algorithms to model the fitness of variants and to design new functional intrinsically disordered proteins." Report summary, verbatim: "Despite our best efforts the phenotype of the target genes previously published by another lab could never be reproduced so we decided to work on different genes. ... Our collaborators at the Kondrashov lab shared a dataset similar to the one we plan to obtain (mutations versus phenotype). The results of this study were published, and the pipeline developed for this data is fully reusable on disordered proteins."

Nearest excluded projects, with the text that excludes them:

The work plan foresees the exploitation of natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins), loaded/expressed in gametes/cells, before drying." On-theme for drying survival but the aim is dry biobanking, not identifying sequence features of unfolded proteins. OUT.
- 749537 DRYSTORE - "We aim to elucidate the effects of drying on DNA structure and function ... using fibroblast as a model cell." DNA integrity in dried cells, no protein-sequence work. OUT.
- 823746 RESIST - "we will study the genomes of several resurrection species and compare them with the genomes of desiccation-sensitive plants." Plants, comparative genomics, not proteins without fixed structure. OUT.
- 725998 RHEA - desiccation appears only as "their desiccation resistance and the associated DNA double-strand breaks"; the project is about asexual genome evolution in bdelloid rotifers. OUT.
- 101030961 DEEPCONSTRUCT and 883742 MUTANOMICS use the same deep-mutagenesis method but on prion condensates and in-vivo protein structure, with no water-loss content. OUT.

record.text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
record.reference_answer: Both projects treat the protective power as something written into the sequence itself and go after it with very large libraries plus machine learning. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which turn into vitrified solids by glass-transition and gelation and so stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and clumping; it computes the sequence features of known CAHS proteins, designs a library that samples that sequence space, screens it with a high-throughput survival assay, checks hits in vitro and in vivo, and feeds the results to machine-learning algorithms to extract the features behind protective glass-transition and then design a fresh library. FLINDIP attacks the same sequence-to-function link from the mutation side, building cell libraries that express hundreds of thousands of variants of tardigrade proteins needed to survive complete drying and scoring every variant by competition assay, again with machine learning used to model variant fitness and design new functional disordered proteins. FLINDIP reported that the phenotype of its original target genes, published by another lab, could never be reproduced, so it moved to different genes, and its delivered result so far is a reusable machine-learning analysis pipeline built on a similar mutation-versus-phenotype dataset from the Kondrashov lab.

evidence:
Gold 838945 - acronym "Desiccation Survival", title "Discovery of intrinsically disordered sequences conferring desiccation survival". Objective, verbatim: "Desiccation is a form of stress wherein extremely dry conditions cause intracellular proteins to unfold and aggregate irreversibly, resulting in cell-death. ... Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins, a family of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in tardigrades (a phylum of micro-animals), have been shown to be important for their survival during long periods of dryness. Under desiccation condition, CAHS proteins undergo glass-transition and gelation to form vitrified solids that protect intracellular proteins from unfolding and aggregation. However, the features of CAHS proteins that confer protection are unknown. Here, I aim to unravel the sequence determinants of CAHS protein functions ... I will (i) perform computational analysis of existing CAHS proteins to extract their sequence features to design a library for adequate sampling of the sequence space; (ii) screen the library with a high-throughput survival-based assay and validate the hits both in vitro and in vivo; (iii) analyse the results with machine learning algorithms to generate characteristic sequence features underlying protective glass-transition. The learned features will be tested by rationally designing and screening a new sequence library for desiccation survival."

Gold 898203 - acronym "FLINDIP", title "Fitness landscape of intrinsically disordered proteins". Objective, verbatim: "The aim of this project is to experimentally measure and analyse, for the first time, the genotype-to-phenotype connection for several intrinsically disordered proteins by deep mutational scanning. We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation. We plan to generate libraries of cells expressing hundreds of thousands of variants of these proteins and to perform competition assays to measure functionality of every variant in the library. We will then use a variety of approaches to analyse the dataset, including machine-learning algorithms to model the fitness of variants and to design new functional intrinsically disordered proteins." Report summary, verbatim: "Despite our best efforts the phenotype of the target genes previously published by another lab could never be reproduced so we decided to work on different genes. ... Our collaborators at the Kondrashov lab shared a dataset similar to the one we plan to obtain (mutations versus phenotype). The results of this study were published, and the pipeline developed for this data is fully reusable on disordered proteins."

findings.claim: The reference says FLINDIP is "building cell libraries that express hundreds of thousands of variants of tardigrade proteins needed to survive complete drying" and that its delivered result is "a reusable machine-learning analysis pipeline built on a similar mutation-versus-phenotype dataset from the Kondrashov lab". FLINDIP's own report says the tardigrade targets were dropped and the shared dataset was four green fluorescent proteins - ordered, folded proteins with no connection to water loss - so the reference's "similar" hides the one fact that decides whether a system's answer is right.
findings.evidence: report_text.workPerformed, verbatim: "In parallel we attempted to reproduce the results of Boothby et al 2017 but could never observe the reported phenotype. ... When lab work resumed we chose to investigate desiccation-resistance proteins from the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family published in Liu et al., 2019. ... We are near finishing the preparation of the new libraries." and "Our collaborators at the Kondrashov lab shared a dataset of mutants vs phenotype for 4 green fluorescent proteins (GFPs). The results were published (Sommermeyer et al., 2022) ... In the paper, we characterized the fitness peaks of four GFPs". finalResults adds "The experimental work planned in the frame of this project on intrinsically disordered proteins of could not be completed by the end of the grant". record.text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
record.reference_answer: Both projects treat the protective power as something written into the sequence itself and go after it with very large libraries plus machine learning. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which turn into vitrified solids by glass-transition and gelation and so stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and clumping; it computes the sequence features of known CAHS proteins, designs a library that samples that sequence space, screens it with a high-throughput survival assay, checks hits in vitro and in vivo, and feeds the results to machine-learning algorithms to extract the features behind protective glass-transition and then design a fresh library. FLINDIP attacks the same sequence-to-function link from the mutation side, building cell libraries that express hundreds of thousands of variants of tardigrade proteins needed to survive complete drying and scoring every variant by competition assay, again with machine learning used to model variant fitness and design new functional disordered proteins. FLINDIP reported that the phenotype of its original target genes, published by another lab, could never be reproduced, so it moved to different genes, and its delivered result so far is a reusable machine-learning analysis pipeline built on a similar mutation-versus-phenotype dataset from the Kondrashov lab.

evidence:
Gold 838945 - acronym "Desiccation Survival", title "Discovery of intrinsically disordered sequences conferring desiccation survival". Objective, verbatim: "Desiccation is a form of stress wherein extremely dry conditions cause intracellular proteins to unfold and aggregate irreversibly, resulting in cell-death. ... Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins, a family of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in tardigrades (a phylum of micro-animals), have been shown to be important for their survival during long periods of dryness. Under desiccation condition, CAHS proteins undergo glass-transition and gelation to form vitrified solids that protect intracellular proteins from unfolding and aggregation. However, the features of CAHS proteins that confer protection are unknown. Here, I aim to unravel the sequence determinants of CAHS protein functions ... I will (i) perform computational analysis of existing CAHS proteins to extract their sequence features to design a library for adequate sampling of the sequence space; (ii) screen the library with a high-throughput survival-based assay and validate the hits both in vitro and in vivo; (iii) analyse the results with machine learning algorithms to generate characteristic sequence features underlying protective glass-transition. The learned features will be tested by rationally designing and screening a new sequence library for desiccation survival."

Gold 898203 - acronym "FLINDIP", title "Fitness landscape of intrinsically disordered proteins". Objective, verbatim: "The aim of this project is to experimentally measure and analyse, for the first time, the genotype-to-phenotype connection for several intrinsically disordered proteins by deep mutational scanning. We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation. We plan to generate libraries of cells expressing hundreds of thousands of variants of these proteins and to perform competition assays to measure functionality of every variant in the library. We will then use a variety of approaches to analyse the dataset, including machine-learning algorithms to model the fitness of variants and to design new functional intrinsically disordered proteins." Report summary, verbatim: "Despite our best efforts the phenotype of the target genes previously published by another lab could never be reproduced so we decided to work on different genes. ... Our collaborators at the Kondrashov lab shared a dataset similar to the one we plan to obtain (mutations versus phenotype). The results of this study were published, and the pipeline developed for this data is fully reusable on disordered proteins."

Nearest excluded projects, with the text that excludes them:
- 734434 DRYNET - "DRYNET's relies on water subtraction to induce a reversible block of metabolism, a survival strategy available in nature (anhydrobiosis). The work plan foresees the exploitation of natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins), loaded/expressed in gametes/cells, before drying." On-theme for drying survival but the aim is dry biobanking, not identifying sequence features of unfolded proteins. OUT.
- 749537 DRYSTORE - "We aim to elucidate the effects of drying on DNA structure and function ... using fibroblast as a model cell." DNA integrity in dried cells, no protein-sequence work. OUT.
- 823746 RESIST - "we will study the genomes of several resurrection species and compare them with the genomes of desiccation-sensitive plants." Plants, comparative genomics, not proteins without fixed structure. OUT.
- 725998 RHEA - desiccation appears only as "their desiccation resistance and the associated DNA double-strand breaks"; the project is about asexual genome evolution in bdelloid rotifers. OUT.
- 101030961 DEEPCONSTRUCT and 883742 MUTANOMICS use the same deep-mutagenesis method but on prion condensates and in-vivo protein structure, with no water-loss content. OUT.

Executed sweep result (b), verbatim rows: objective ILIKE ('intrinsically disordered'|'disordered protein'|'unstructured protein'|CAHS|'glass transition'|vitrif) AND (desicc|dry|dehydrat|'water loss'|anhydro) -> 2 rows: 838945 "Desiccation Survival"; 898203 "FLINDIP". Drift check on the candidate evidence -> n_all=4, n_label=1, unchanged.
why_good: The question separates conditions that can bridge plain-language phrasing to two very differently written texts: neither gold project is reachable by lexical search at k=20, and the only lexically obvious wording ("desiccation tolerance") matches a single, different project. It fills natural-sciences / biological-sciences on the vector L2 synthesis cell with a paraphrase term_style, an axis combination the promoted bank does not yet carry. The L2 label is arithmetic: exhaustive SQL sweeps over drying vocabulary and over every disordered-protein project in the corpus leave exactly two projects that ask what a sequence must contain to protect through drying, and the answer is a single account - library plus survival/fitness measurement plus machine learning - that neither project states on its own.

record.text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
record.reference_answer: Both projects treat protection against drying as something encoded in the sequence of proteins that never adopt a fixed structure, and both planned the same combination - large libraries of sequence variants, a score per variant, and machine learning to extract the rules - but each report records how far that plan actually got. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which under drying undergo glass-transition and gelation into vitrified solids that stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and aggregating, and planned computational analysis of known CAHS sequences, a designed library screened by a high-throughput survival assay, and machine-learning extraction of the features behind protective glass-transition; what its report describes as executed is an integrative analytical pipeline combining computational sequence analysis, structural characterization using NMR, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, through which it identified new protein sequences and features contributing to desiccation survival and uncovered the mechanism by which these IDPs achieve stress tolerance - the survival screen and the machine-learning step are not mentioned there. FLINDIP planned deep mutational scanning of tardigrade proteins essential for surviving complete desiccation, with cell libraries of hundreds of thousands of variants scored by competition assay; its report states that random-mutant libraries for the original target genes were built but the phenotype of Boothby et al 2017 could never be reproduced, so after the Covid-19 closure the work switched to desiccation-resistance proteins of the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family from Liu et al., 2019, whose repeat-rich sequences complicated synthesis and whose new libraries were near finishing preparation at grant end, and that the planned experimental work on intrinsically disordered proteins could not be completed by the end of the grant. FLINDIP's analysis half did deliver: the reusable pipeline was built and demonstrated on a Kondrashov lab dataset of mutants versus phenotype for four green fluorescent proteins (GFPs), published as Sommermeyer et al., 2022, whose finding was that mutationally robust proteins are not optimal templates for machine-learning-driven protein design and that predictions are more accurate for mutationally fragile proteins.

All four seeds were read in full. evidence:
Gold 838945 - acronym "Desiccation Survival", title "Discovery of intrinsically disordered sequences conferring desiccation survival".
Objective, verbatim: "Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins, a family of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in tardigrades (a phylum of micro-animals), have been shown to be important for their survival during long periods of dryness. Under desiccation condition, CAHS proteins undergo glass-transition and gelation to form vitrified solids that protect intracellular proteins from unfolding and aggregation. However, the features of CAHS proteins that confer protection are unknown. Here, I aim to unravel the sequence determinants of CAHS protein functions ... I will (i) perform computational analysis of existing CAHS proteins to extract their sequence features to design a library for adequate sampling of the sequence space; (ii) screen the library with a high-throughput survival-based assay and validate the hits both in vitro and in vivo; (iii) analyse the results with machine learning algorithms to generate characteristic sequence features underlying protective glass-transition."
Report workPerformed, verbatim and in full: "Through development of an integrative analytical pipeline, combining computational sequence analysis, structural characterization using NMR, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, I successfully identified new protein sequences and features that could contribute to desiccation survival and abiotic stress tolerance in general. I also uncovered the mechanism by which these IDPs achieve stress tolerance."

Gold 898203 - acronym "FLINDIP", title "Fitness landscape of intrinsically disordered proteins".
Objective, verbatim: "The aim of this project is to experimentally measure and analyse, for the first time, the genotype-to-phenotype connection for several intrinsically disordered proteins by deep mutational scanning. We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation. We plan to generate libraries of cells expressing hundreds of thousands of variants of these proteins and to perform competition assays to measure functionality of every variant in the library."
Report workPerformed, verbatim: "We used the optimised sequence as template in error-prone PCR to generate libraries of random mutants. ... In parallel we attempted to reproduce the results of Boothby et al 2017 but could never observe the reported phenotype. At this point, our lab closed due to Covid-19. When lab work resumed we chose to investigate desiccation-resistance proteins from the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family published in Liu et al., 2019. These sequences are extremely rich in repeated regions, which creates difficulties for gene synthesis, assembly and sequencing. Still, our preliminary experiments with these genes showed a promising phenotype in bacteria. We are near finishing the preparation of the new libraries. ... Our collaborators at the Kondrashov lab shared a dataset of mutants vs phenotype for 4 green fluorescent proteins (GFPs). The results were published (Sommermeyer et al., 2022) and the code, available on Github can be reused on intrinsically disordered proteins. ... Interestingly, mutationally robust proteins are not optimal templates for machine-learning-driven protein design. Instead, predictions were more accurate for mutationally fragile proteins."
Report finalResults, verbatim: "The experimental work planned in the frame of this project on intrinsically disordered proteins of could not be completed by the end of the grant, but it shows promising progress."

record.text: A project set out to work out how often rivers across Spain and neighbouring parts of southwestern Europe burst their banks and caused serious damage, going back hundreds to thousands of years before gauge measurements began, by reading the bands of mud that had settled on lake bottoms. How did its researchers work out which of those buried bands had been laid down by such an event?
record.reference_answer: The project (FLOODARC) worked from sediment cores and geochemical and chronological datasets that were already available for the studied Iberian sites: it started with descriptions of those cores, then prepared thin sections and applied a state-of-the-art protocol that combined detailed microfacies analyses with geochemical analyses to identify the flood layers. The flood records it analysed span from the last centuries in the Western Ebro Basin (NE Spain) to the last 26000 years in NW Spain.

record.text: Which research projects study the Viking Age in Scandinavia and the Norse world, roughly 750 to 1050 AD, as a period their own research covers, as opposed to projects whose stated subject lies mainly earlier, in the Scandinavian Iron Age or prehistory, or mainly later, in the Christian medieval or early modern North?
record.reference_answer: Five projects cover the Viking Age itself, and they reach it from very different evidence. SILVER attacks the origins of the Viking Age (c. 750-1050 AD) through an interdisciplinary archaeological, archaeometric and numismatic study of silver from early Viking-Age Scandinavia, asking where, when and why the period began. GENTES re-examines the contemporary and near-contemporary written sources for Scandinavia c. 750-c. 1000 and argues that its history should not rest on the 13th-century Icelandic Sagas. BODY-POLITICS combines aDNA, isotope analyses and osteobiography with social theory to study personhood, sexuality and death in the Scandinavian Iron and Viking Ages, building the first synthesising dataset of human remains deposited in settlements. IPACE applies three-dimensional cranial shape analysis to ask who settled Iceland in the 9th to 10th centuries and whether that colonisation involved the Viking slave trade. SYMBODIN takes pre-Christian myth and ritual as its starting point and traces bodily metaphors in Old Norse myth from the Viking Age through the transition to Christianity. Numismatics, source criticism, osteoarchaeology, physical anthropology and the study of myth converge on one period.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-26 (657128, 792006, 797386, 802349, 949886), re-executed this pass: the fenced SQL (euroSciVoc 'humanities/history and archaeology%' AND lower(objective) LIKE '%viking%') still returns exactly those 5. INCLUSION RULE (both edges fenced, applicable from a single project's own text): the project's own stated period of study must cover the Viking-Age window c. 750-1050 substantially rather than merely touching one of its edges, and must not be centred before it (Scandinavian Iron Age / prehistory) or after it (Christian medieval, early modern North); the region must be Scandinavia or the Norse world. Applied per project, using the project's own dating: 802349 SILVER states 'c. 750-1050 AD' - the window exactly - IN. 792006 GENTES states 'c. 750 and c. 1000' - covers 250 of the 300 window years - IN. 748200 IPACE states 'the main period of migration taking place from the 9th to 10th centuries' and 'the Viking slave trade' - inside the window - IN. 949886 BODY-POLITICS states 'the Scandinavian Iron and Viking Ages' and 'first millennium Northern Europe', and its report reports 'human remains deposited in settlements in Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia' - its stated span runs to the end of the first millennium, covering c. 750-1000 of the window, and the Viking Age is one of the two periods it names as its subject - IN (decided explicitly). 750379 SYMBODIN's title states 'from the Viking Age to Late Medieval Times' and its objective makes pre-Christian myth and ritual the starting point, so it enters the window at its start rather than sitting after it - IN. 797386 ArcNames states 'Scandinavia, ca. 300 - 800 AD' and its report calls the material 'Scandinavian Iron Age personal names' and 'personal names from the late Scandinavian prehistory... beginning from the Roman Iron Age'; its stated span touches only the first 50 years of the window and is centred four centuries earlier - OUT (dropped from gold this round). 657128 LEXICON POETICUM's report dates its corpus 'composed between the 9th and 14th centuries by poets from Norway and its settlements throughout Europe, especially Iceland', so more of its material falls after 1050 than inside the window and the project is lexicography of the whole Old Norse corpus - OUT (dropped from gold this round). Other pool adjudications, all OUT: 654147 Invisibilia (manuscripts ca. 1100-1500), 654860 TRANSLATIS (Latin-to-Old-Norse translation in medieval Iceland, after the arrival of Christian literacy), 658110 NORNS (vernacular romance and historiography, 13th-15th century), 839290 LangMix (medieval Scandinavia after Latin script arrives), 707946 Forgery (17th-18th century saga forgeries), 890522 SunSHINE (Proto-Indo-European poetics and Bronze Age artefacts), 896809 OutNorth (c.1400-1900), 840531 HANSEALTAR (fifteenth century), 715626 LatinNow (north-western Roman Empire), 657211 TEMPI (prehistoric Italy c.4500-2000 BC), 851511 MICROSCOPE (pre-Roman European Iron Age, 'Celtic' core region, third century BC), 101002357 RELEVEN (late 11th century c. 1030-1095, eastern Christendom), 750353 BioTec (the Viking Mars lander of the 1970s), 895153 WINDOWGLASSMED (7th-10th century glass but western Europe, not the Norse world), 669461 NorFish (1400-1700), 724317 ARCTIC CULT (modern collecting), 842612 Sus.Post-Med (late medieval to early modern pig husbandry), 856488 SEACHANGE (marine baselines over 2,000-8,000 years, despite a Viking-Age Iceland work package), 893072 BONEZ (Eastern Baltic, 1st to 13th AD, not the Norse world). record.text: Some proteins have no fixed folded structure, yet proteins of this kind are what carry certain tiny animals and their cells through the loss of virtually all their water. How are EU-funded projects working out which features of such a protein's amino-acid sequence provide that protection?
record.reference_answer: Both projects treat protection against drying as something encoded in the sequence of proteins that never adopt a fixed structure, and both planned the same combination - large libraries of sequence variants, a score per variant, and machine learning to extract the rules - but each report records how far that plan actually got. The Desiccation Survival project starts from Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins of tardigrades, which under drying undergo glass-transition and gelation into vitrified solids that stop the cell's other proteins unfolding and aggregating, and planned computational analysis of known CAHS sequences, a designed library screened by a high-throughput survival assay, and machine-learning extraction of the features behind protective glass-transition; what its report describes as executed is an integrative analytical pipeline combining computational sequence analysis, structural characterization using NMR, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, through which it identified new protein sequences and features contributing to desiccation survival and uncovered the mechanism by which these IDPs achieve stress tolerance - the survival screen and the machine-learning step are not mentioned there. FLINDIP planned deep mutational scanning of tardigrade proteins essential for surviving complete desiccation, with cell libraries of hundreds of thousands of variants scored by competition assay; its report states that random-mutant libraries for the original target genes were built but the phenotype of Boothby et al 2017 could never be reproduced, so after the Covid-19 closure the work switched to desiccation-resistance proteins of the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family from Liu et al., 2019, whose repeat-rich sequences complicated synthesis and whose new libraries were near finishing preparation at grant end, and that the planned experimental work on intrinsically disordered proteins could not be completed by the end of the grant. FLINDIP's analysis half did deliver: the reusable pipeline was built and demonstrated on a Kondrashov lab dataset of mutants versus phenotype for four green fluorescent proteins (GFPs), published as Sommermeyer et al., 2022, whose finding was that mutationally robust proteins are not optimal templates for machine-learning-driven protein design and that predictions are more accurate for mutationally fragile proteins.

evidence:
Gold 838945 - acronym "Desiccation Survival", title "Discovery of intrinsically disordered sequences conferring desiccation survival".
Objective, verbatim: "Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins, a family of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in tardigrades (a phylum of micro-animals), have been shown to be important for their survival during long periods of dryness. Under desiccation condition, CAHS proteins undergo glass-transition and gelation to form vitrified solids that protect intracellular proteins from unfolding and aggregation. However, the features of CAHS proteins that confer protection are unknown. Here, I aim to unravel the sequence determinants of CAHS protein functions ... I will (i) perform computational analysis of existing CAHS proteins to extract their sequence features to design a library for adequate sampling of the sequence space; (ii) screen the library with a high-throughput survival-based assay and validate the hits both in vitro and in vivo; (iii) analyse the results with machine learning algorithms to generate characteristic sequence features underlying protective glass-transition."
Report workPerformed, verbatim and in full: "Through development of an integrative analytical pipeline, combining computational sequence analysis, structural characterization using NMR, solution biophysics and ensemble generation, membrane biophysics, yeast genetics and cell biology, I successfully identified new protein sequences and features that could contribute to desiccation survival and abiotic stress tolerance in general. I also uncovered the mechanism by which these IDPs achieve stress tolerance."

Gold 898203 - acronym "FLINDIP", title "Fitness landscape of intrinsically disordered proteins".
Objective, verbatim: "The aim of this project is to experimentally measure and analyse, for the first time, the genotype-to-phenotype connection for several intrinsically disordered proteins by deep mutational scanning. We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation. We plan to generate libraries of cells expressing hundreds of thousands of variants of these proteins and to perform competition assays to measure functionality of every variant in the library."
Report workPerformed, verbatim: "We used the optimised sequence as template in error-prone PCR to generate libraries of random mutants. ... In parallel we attempted to reproduce the results of Boothby et al 2017 but could never observe the reported phenotype. At this point, our lab closed due to Covid-19. When lab work resumed we chose to investigate desiccation-resistance proteins from the Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) family published in Liu et al., 2019. These sequences are extremely rich in repeated regions, which creates difficulties for gene synthesis, assembly and sequencing. Still, our preliminary experiments with these genes showed a promising phenotype in bacteria. We are near finishing the preparation of the new libraries. ... Our collaborators at the Kondrashov lab shared a dataset of mutants vs phenotype for 4 green fluorescent proteins (GFPs). The results were published (Sommermeyer et al., 2022) and the code, available on Github can be reused on intrinsically disordered proteins. ... Interestingly, mutationally robust proteins are not optimal templates for machine-learning-driven protein design. Instead, predictions were more accurate for mutationally fragile proteins."
Report finalResults, verbatim: "The experimental work planned in the frame of this project on intrinsically disordered proteins of could not be completed by the end of the grant, but it shows promising progress."

judge_decisions.rationale: The cell holds: the question measures whether a system can find two independent projects attacking the sequence-to-function link in desiccation-protective disordered proteins and synthesize their shared method (large designed/mutational libraries plus machine learning), and the critic's own missed-gold hunt confirms |gold|=2 and both golds' fit. What is broken is the scoring artifact, not the question - the reference presents FLINDIP's planned tardigrade library and a vaguely "similar" dataset as delivered results, so a system that reads FLINDIP's report and answers accurately is scored down for being right. Direction: separate what FLINDIP planned from what its report says it did, keep the deep-mutational-scanning-plus-machine-learning approach since that is what the question measures, and apply the same plan-versus-report discipline to 838945.

The question still measures exactly what its cell claims: a vector L2 synthesis over two independently retrieved projects that both attack the sequence-to-function link in desiccation-protective disordered proteins with large variant libraries plus machine learning, with gold, level, subtype, term_style and pooling all re-executed unchanged this round and the round-1 reference defect cleared. The one surviving MID is length and scope in the scoring artifact, not a wrong or unsupported claim - a system that answers the method question well is graded against a reference whose tail carries true but unasked project-history and publication content. That degrades a score at the margin; it does not move the entry into the wrong cell or punish a system for being right about a fact the reference contradicts, which is what would make it the HIGH it is not. The fix round is spent, and discarding a question whose gold is sound and independently re-verified in order to draft a fresh candidate from scratch would cost the bank more than the note costs it. No stop rule triggered.

record.text: Which research projects study the Viking Age in Scandinavia and the Norse world, roughly 750 to 1050 AD, as a period their own research covers, as opposed to projects whose stated subject lies mainly earlier, in the Scandinavian Iron Age or prehistory, or mainly later, in the Christian medieval or early modern North?
record.reference_answer: Five projects cover the Viking Age itself, and they reach it from very different evidence. SILVER attacks the origins of the Viking Age (c. 750-1050 AD) through an interdisciplinary archaeological, archaeometric and numismatic study of silver from early Viking-Age Scandinavia, asking where, when and why the period began. GENTES re-examines the contemporary and near-contemporary written sources for Scandinavia c. 750-c. 1000 and argues that its history should not rest on the 13th-century Icelandic Sagas. BODY-POLITICS combines aDNA, isotope analyses and osteobiography with social theory to study personhood, sexuality and death in the Scandinavian Iron and Viking Ages, building the first synthesising dataset of human remains deposited in settlements. IPACE applies three-dimensional cranial shape analysis to ask who settled Iceland in the 9th to 10th centuries and whether that colonisation involved the Viking slave trade. SYMBODIN takes pre-Christian myth and ritual as its starting point and traces bodily metaphors in Old Norse myth from the Viking Age through the transition to Christianity. Numismatics, source criticism, osteoarchaeology, physical anthropology and the study of myth converge on one period.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-26 (657128, 792006, 797386, 802349, 949886), re-executed this pass: the fenced SQL (euroSciVoc 'humanities/history and archaeology%' AND lower(objective) LIKE '%viking%') still returns exactly those 5. INCLUSION RULE (both edges fenced, applicable from a single project's own text): the project's own stated period of study must cover the Viking-Age window c. 750-1050 substantially rather than merely touching one of its edges, and must not be centred before it (Scandinavian Iron Age / prehistory) or after it (Christian medieval, early modern North); the region must be Scandinavia or the Norse world. record.text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects treat water with a constructed wetland of their own. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX integrates anaerobic ammonia-oxidising, anode-respiring bacteria into METlands to strip nitrogen from sewage; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 sites; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm retention and nutrient-recovery measures; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.

why_good: The question discriminates on a boundary that no stored field encodes: whether a project's own text names a constructed wetland it builds, pilots or tests, as opposed to a natural wetland it studies. Systems that lean on the euroSciVoc environmental-engineering tag find 5 of the 13; systems that lean on the exact phrase in objectives find 6; the other 7 gold projects only surface from report text (ELECTRA, PAVITRA GANGA, HYDROUSA, M2EX, INNOV, INDIA-H2O, NICE), so recall separates the conditions sharply while precision is tested by three near-miss projects that use the same words (UMIC, MULTISOURCE, OPTWET). It fills the environmental-engineering / water-treatment axis of the frontier, which no existing vector entry occupies, at exact-term style. The L3 label is arithmetic: 13 read-verified gold projects against a floor of 5.

record.text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects treat water with a constructed wetland of their own. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX integrates anaerobic ammonia-oxidising, anode-respiring bacteria into METlands to strip nitrogen from sewage; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 sites; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm retention and nutrient-recovery measures; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.

record.text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects treat water with a constructed wetland of their own. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX integrates anaerobic ammonia-oxidising, anode-respiring bacteria into METlands to strip nitrogen from sewage; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment across 13 sites; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm retention and nutrient-recovery measures; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.

record.text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
record.reference_answer: Fourteen projects put a planted wetland bed of their own to work on water. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX reported constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material recovering nitrogen from source-separated urine, reaching NH4+ oxidation rates up to 284 mg N/L/d but only 43% N recovery; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands combined with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment as one of the natural-engineered combinations spread over its 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, which also cover bank filtration and managed aquifer recharge; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm water retention and nutrient-recovery measures; DIVAGRI co-develops an artificial wetland with smallholders as one of seven bio-based technologies installed at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites in Sub-Saharan Africa, a water-saving technology alongside its sub-surface clay-based irrigation system; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.

MEMBERSHIP RULE (the axis, not the string): a project is IN when it installs, pilots or tests a planted wetland bed OF ITS OWN as a working unit handling a water stream - sewage, greywater, stormwater, groundwater, source-separated urine, farm drainage or runoff, or irrigation water - whatever word the project uses for it (constructed, artificial, treatment, METland, hybrid subsurface wetland). The wetland need NOT treat a named wastewater stream, and the literal word 'constructed' is not load-bearing. A project is OUT when it only studies, models, monitors, restores or writes about wetlands, or when a wetland it did not build is merely the setting or the motivation. Applied to the two agricultural cases in the same breath: 858375 WATERAGRI is IN - objective O4 'identify, develop and test affordable ... farm solutions such as ... farm constructed wetlands', report 'exploring nature-based methods (farm-constructed wetlands, controlled drainage, bio-inspired filters)' - a planted bed it develops and tests for on-farm water retention and nutrient recovery, not for sewage; 101000348 DIVAGRI is IN on exactly that rule - report summary 'Biotechnologies co-developed with smallholders at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites across the continent include a desalination greenhouse, artificial wetland, biogas digester, biochar kiln, a subsurface irrigation system, mobile biorefinery and intercropping', workPerformed 'Water saving technologies such as artificial wetlands and a sub-surface clay-based irrigation system have already caught the attention of farmers in the co-design phase ... All seven bio-based technologies will be installed at all pilot sites within the next few months'. Neither treats a named wastewater stream; both install a planted wetland bed of their own; they fall together. Other adjudications - IN: 642190 iMETland (METland units constructed and operated), 894525 ELECTRAMMOX (constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material, applied to N recovery from source-separated urine, 284 mg N/L/d oxidation, 43% recovery), 826244 ELECTRA ('solutions were relying on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands for wastewater treatment'), 689450 AquaNES (demonstrates CW plus engineered pre/post treatment), 773351 ZIRONITRO (a constructed wetland producing nitrate-free drinking water), 689242 INCOVER ('The sludge treatment wetland produced good quality soil conditioner'), 101003765 NICE (pilots 'designed, constructed & integrated', 'such as vertical gardens, constructed wetl&s, & rain gardens'), 776643 HYDROUSA ('Coupling anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands (CWs) and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection'), 821051 PAVITRA GANGA ('Constructed Wetlands + Technology: combining vertical subsurface flow CW with granular activated carbon and zeolite ... advancing from TRL 4 to TRL 6'), 861088 M2EX ('constructed wetlands (CWs) were employed to treat the resulting effluent'; 'ESR14 evaluated the potential of constructed wetlands (CWs) to recover/remove metals from wastewater/digestate'), 739732 INNOV ('Using constructed wetland technologies, alchemia-nova is developing indoor and outdoor plant-based applications, to treat such contaminated water for household reuse'), 820906 INDIA-H2O ('The treatment capacity has been validated in a small wetland construction and larger a larger scale solution has been constructed and will be installed and to treat the wastewater source at PDEU'). record.text: Which projects build, pilot or test constructed wetlands - engineered planted treatment beds such as subsurface-flow wetlands, sludge treatment wetlands or microbial-electrochemical METlands - as part of their own water or wastewater treatment work, rather than only studying, modelling or restoring natural wetlands?
record.reference_answer: Fourteen projects put a planted wetland bed of their own to work on water. One group builds electro-enhanced wetlands: iMETland constructed and operated full-scale METland units - electroconductive biofilter beds worked by electroactive bacteria - for zero-energy urban wastewater treatment in small communities; ELECTRAMMOX reported constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material recovering nitrogen from source-separated urine, reaching NH4+ oxidation rates up to 284 mg N/L/d but only 43% N recovery; ELECTRA's solutions relied on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands, whose bed materials and electron-sink control improved removal of pharmaceutical residues from raw and secondary effluent. A second group uses the wetland as one stage of a larger train: AquaNES demonstrated constructed wetlands combined with ozone or bioreactor pre- and post-treatment as one of the natural-engineered combinations spread over its 13 demonstration sites in Europe, India and Israel, which also cover bank filtration and managed aquifer recharge; PAVITRA GANGA piloted 'Constructed Wetlands +', a vertical subsurface flow CW combined with granular activated carbon and zeolite, from TRL 4 to TRL 6 in India; HYDROUSA coupled anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands and UV disinfection on three Greek islands; INCOVER's sludge treatment wetland yielded a soil conditioner meeting Spanish heavy-metal rules. The rest run wetlands as the core technology or as one tested option: ZIRONITRO is a constructed wetland removing 98% of nitrates from contaminated groundwater to make drinking water; INNOV automates alchemia-nova's vertECO indoor constructed-wetland unit for greywater reuse; NICE designed and constructed 15 pilots at 10 urban sites, among them constructed wetlands and rain gardens for stormwater, greywater and wastewater; INDIA-H2O validated its phyto-treatment capacity in a small wetland construction and built a larger one for wastewater at PDEU; WATERAGRI identifies, develops and tests farm constructed wetlands among its on-farm water retention and nutrient-recovery measures; DIVAGRI co-develops an artificial wetland with smallholders as one of seven bio-based technologies installed at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites in Sub-Saharan Africa, a water-saving technology alongside its sub-surface clay-based irrigation system; and in M2EX constructed wetlands were employed to treat digestate effluent and evaluated for recovering metals from wastewater.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-64 (constructed wetlands): 642190, 689450, 701542, 773351, 858375, 894525; the candidate's SQL (objective/title ILIKE '%constructed wetland%') re-executed in the drafting pass and still returns exactly those 6. MEMBERSHIP RULE (the axis, not the string): a project is IN when it installs, pilots or tests a planted wetland bed OF ITS OWN as a working unit handling a water stream - sewage, greywater, stormwater, groundwater, source-separated urine, farm drainage or runoff, or irrigation water - whatever word the project uses for it (constructed, artificial, treatment, METland, hybrid subsurface wetland). The wetland need NOT treat a named wastewater stream, and the literal word 'constructed' is not load-bearing. A project is OUT when it only studies, models, monitors, restores or writes about wetlands, or when a wetland it did not build is merely the setting or the motivation. Applied to the two agricultural cases in the same breath: 858375 WATERAGRI is IN - objective O4 'identify, develop and test affordable ... farm solutions such as ... farm constructed wetlands', report 'exploring nature-based methods (farm-constructed wetlands, controlled drainage, bio-inspired filters)' - a planted bed it develops and tests for on-farm water retention and nutrient recovery, not for sewage; 101000348 DIVAGRI is IN on exactly that rule - report summary 'Biotechnologies co-developed with smallholders at 12 pilot and 15 demonstration sites across the continent include a desalination greenhouse, artificial wetland, biogas digester, biochar kiln, a subsurface irrigation system, mobile biorefinery and intercropping', workPerformed 'Water saving technologies such as artificial wetlands and a sub-surface clay-based irrigation system have already caught the attention of farmers in the co-design phase ... All seven bio-based technologies will be installed at all pilot sites within the next few months'. Neither treats a named wastewater stream; both install a planted wetland bed of their own; they fall together. Other adjudications - IN: 642190 iMETland (METland units constructed and operated), 894525 ELECTRAMMOX (constructed wetlands packed with electroconductive carrier material, applied to N recovery from source-separated urine, 284 mg N/L/d oxidation, 43% recovery), 826244 ELECTRA ('solutions were relying on electrochemically enhanced constructed wetlands for wastewater treatment'), 689450 AquaNES (demonstrates CW plus engineered pre/post treatment), 773351 ZIRONITRO (a constructed wetland producing nitrate-free drinking water), 689242 INCOVER ('The sludge treatment wetland produced good quality soil conditioner'), 101003765 NICE (pilots 'designed, constructed & integrated', 'such as vertical gardens, constructed wetl&s, & rain gardens'), 776643 HYDROUSA ('Coupling anaerobic processes with constructed wetlands (CWs) and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection'), 821051 PAVITRA GANGA ('Constructed Wetlands + Technology: combining vertical subsurface flow CW with granular activated carbon and zeolite ... advancing from TRL 4 to TRL 6'), 861088 M2EX ('constructed wetlands (CWs) were employed to treat the resulting effluent'; 'ESR14 evaluated the potential of constructed wetlands (CWs) to recover/remove metals from wastewater/digestate'), 739732 INNOV ('Using constructed wetland technologies, alchemia-nova is developing indoor and outdoor plant-based applications, to treat such contaminated water for household reuse'), 820906 INDIA-H2O ('The treatment capacity has been validated in a small wetland construction and larger a larger scale solution has been constructed and will be installed and to treat the wastewater source at PDEU').
